mcqs.question: Which of the following statements about the interaction between the poles of two magnets is correct?

options.D: Poles do not interact at all

mcqs.explanation: Opposite poles (north and south) always attract each other, while like poles repel. Option C correctly describes this fundamental magnetic interaction. Options A and B describe repulsion between like poles, which is false, and D denies any magnetic force, which is also incorrect.

mcqs.question: If the north pole of one magnet is brought close to the north pole of another magnet, what will happen?

options.C: They will neither attract nor repel
options.D: They will combine into a single pole

mcqs.explanation: Like poles (north‑north or south‑south) exert a repulsive force on each other. Therefore the two north poles push away from each other, making option B correct. Option A describes attraction, which occurs only between opposite poles. Option C is wrong because a magnetic force is always present, and option D is physically impossible.

mcqs.question: Which pair of magnet poles will experience the strongest attractive force?

options.A: North pole of magnet A and north pole of magnet B
options.B: South pole of magnet A and south pole of magnet B
options.C: North pole of magnet A and south pole of magnet B
options.D: No pair will attract; all will repel

mcqs.answer: North pole of magnet A and south pole of magnet B
mcqs.explanation: Unlike poles (north and south) attract each other, producing the magnetic force that pulls the two magnets together. Options A and B describe like‑pole interactions, which are repulsive. Option D is incorrect because attraction does occur between opposite poles. Hence, option C is the correct choice.

mcqs.question: A student wants to identify the north pole of a bar magnet using a known compass. Which experimental step will correctly reveal the north pole of the bar magnet?

options.A: Bring each end of the bar magnet close to the north‑seeking end of the compass needle and note which end attracts it.
options.B: Place a paper clip at each end of the bar magnet and observe which end picks up the clip.
options.C: Suspend the bar magnet freely and see which end points toward the geographic north direction.
options.D: Bring each end of the bar magnet near the north‑seeking end of a second, known magnet and note which end repels it.

mcqs.answer: Bring each end of the bar magnet near the north‑seeking end of a second, known magnet and note which end repels it.
mcqs.explanation: A known magnet’s north pole repels the north pole of another magnet. Therefore, the end of the unknown bar magnet that repels the known north pole is itself a north pole. Option D describes this correct procedure. Option A would identify the south pole (since the compass north‑seeking end is attracted to a magnetic south pole). Option B only shows attraction, not polarity. Option C aligns the magnet with Earth’s magnetic field, which points the magnet’s north pole toward Earth’s magnetic south pole, giving ambiguous results for a classroom experiment.
